## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cunda Sutta* (Ud 8.5) is the fifth discourse in the eighth chapter (*Pāṭaligāmiyavagga*) of the *Udāna*. The sutta narrates the episode of the Buddha's final meal, offered by the metalworker Cunda, which immediately precedes his final illness and parinibbāna. None of the secondary literature passages in the dossier discuss this specific text, as they instead treat other homonymous discourses concerning the elder Mahācunda or the novice Cunda.

 Automated text-reuse data from DharmaNexus confirms this close kinship, showing 174 matching passages with DN 16 spanning over 28,000 characters, with nearly identical phrasing across the meal and illness sequences (§1.2–12.4 matching DN 16 §4.13.4–4.23.3 at 0.96 similarity) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus records extensive shared phrasing with several Vinaya Khandhaka sections, particularly the *Bhesajjakkhandhaka* (Kd 6), and aligns the sutta cross-linguistically with Chinese versions of the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra* (such as T 7), Tibetan Vinaya sections (*vinaya-kṣudraka-vastu*, D0006-2), and Sanskrit *Saṅghabhedavastu* fragments [DharmaNexus]. The episode and its doctrinal ramifications are also cited and discussed in post-canonical works, notably the *Milindapañha* (Mil 5.3.6) and the *Peṭakopadesa* [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
